t: You're standing at a memorial to Alfred Harmsworth, Lord Northcliffe, outside St Dunstan-in-the-West on Fleet Street. He owned the Daily Mail and the Daily Mirror, and he was an early developer of popular journalism, with huge influence over public opinion in Edwardian Britain. Lord Beaverbrook called him the greatest figure who ever strode down Fleet Street, and this is the street. The sculptor was Kathleen Scott, widow of the Antarctic explorer Captain Scott. The architect was Edwin Lutyens, who also designed many war memorials and country houses.
